❌ MYTH: Your bra straps are what hold your bust up.
✅ TRUTH: Straps carry only a small share of the weight — the band does the real work.

When the band is snug and level, most of the support comes from your ribcage. If your straps dig in, the band is probably too loose and the cups too small.

Test it: fasten on the loosest hook, lift your arms, and check whether the band stays level at the back. If it rides up, go down a band size.

❌ MYTH: A new bra should feel tight and "break in" after a few weeks.
✅ TRUTH: A well-fitted bra feels supportive from the first wear — not painful.

A new band can relax slightly, but it should never leave deep marks, dig into your ribs, or need weeks of stretching. Start on the loosest hook so you have room to tighten as the band relaxes.

If it hurts on day one, the size or shape is wrong — not something to "get used to."

❌ MYTH: A 34DD is the same size in every brand.
✅ TRUTH: Cup volume changes with the band — 34DD, 32DDD and 36D can hold similar volume but fit very differently.

That is the sister-size rule: when you go down a band, go up a cup; when you go up a band, go down a cup. Cup volume stays close while the frame changes.

Always check the brand's size chart and your measurements — not just the label.

❌ MYTH: If the underwire pokes, that is just what a supportive bra feels like.
✅ TRUTH: A wire should sit flat against your ribcage and never dig into the armpit or center.

Poking usually means the wire is too narrow, the cup too small, or the band too loose. European seamed cups are built around a narrower wire and deeper projection so the wire follows your natural root.

Check: the center gore should lie flat, and the wire should stay outside your breast tissue.

❌ MYTH: More foam means more support for a full bust.
✅ TRUTH: Support comes from structure, not thickness.

Thick molded cups can gap, push tissue backward, and trap heat. Multi-part seamed cups with a firm band lift and project naturally — with less bulk under your clothes.

Look for seamed construction, side slings and a powernet band instead of extra padding.

❌ MYTH: You measure your bra size once and it stays the same forever.
✅ TRUTH: Your size can change with weight, hormones, age and even a new brand.

Remeasure every 6–12 months, and recheck the band first: it should sit level and snug on the loosest hook. A cup that fit last year may not fit this year.

Keep one well-fitted reference bra and compare new ones against it.

❌ MYTH: A full bust needs a minimizer bra to look good under clothes.
✅ TRUTH: Compression flattens — good structure lifts and smooths.

A minimizer presses tissue flat and can cause bulging at the sides. A well-fitted seamed bra with a firm band and side support gives a natural, lifted shape that looks smooth under clothes without squeezing.

Comfort and a clean line are a fit issue, not a size issue.
